findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime fields used by OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get configures OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", where AuditLogEntry.datetime is a DateTimeField. However, OptimizedCursorPaginator implements get_item_key and value_from_cursor for numeric fields rather than datetime fields: get_item_key passes getattr(item, "datetime") (a datetime.datetime instance) to math.floor() and math.ceil(), raising TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime whenever any audit log entries are returned. In addition, value_from_cursor returns the raw numeric cursor.value instead of converting it back to a timezone-aware datetime object like DateTimePaginator does, which causes the SQL query to fail when comparing the timestamp column against a number.

findings.title: Unconditional access to organization_context.member raises AttributeError when member is None
findings.body: Line 71 evaluates request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access on every GET request to OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint. In RpcUserOrganizationContext, organization_context.member can be None (for example, when authenticating with an organization auth token or API token where request.user is an AnonymousUser and request.user.is_superuser is False). Dereferencing organization_context.member.has_global_access without a None check will raise an unhandled AttributeError (HTTP 500) even when optimized_pagination is not requested. Additionally, Sentry endpoints should check is_active_superuser(request) rather than request.user.is_superuser so inactive superuser sessions do not grant elevated access.

findings.title: Negative cursor.offset slicing on a Django QuerySet raises ValueError and computes invalid slice bounds
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (lines 877-882) and BasePaginator.get_result (lines 182-184), negative offsets are passed directly into queryset[start_offset:stop] when enable_advanced_features is True or cursor.is_prev is True. Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ does not support negative indexing and immediately raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.") whenever start < 0 or stop < 0. Moreover, computing stop = start_offset + limit + extra with a negative start_offset (e.g. -5) and positive limit + extra (e.g. 101) produces a positive stop index (96), resulting in a malformed slice [-5:96] that mixes negative and positive indices.

findings.title: Clamping negative offset to 0 in BasePaginator.get_result corrupts generated cursors
findings.body: In BasePaginator.get_result (line 182) and OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (line 884), start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset silently clamps a negative cursor.offset to 0 when slicing the queryset for forward pagination instead of rejecting the invalid negative offset. Because cursor.offset remains negative when passed into build_cursor, _build_prev_values evaluates has_prev = bool(value or offset) as True even on the first page (value=0), and _build_next_values computes next_offset = offset + limit using the negative offset when page boundary keys are equal.
